title_en: Several Provisions of the State Council on Further Improving Cultural Economic Policies

articles.content_en:
III. Continue Implementing Fiscal and Tax Preferential Policies
With economic development and the growth of fiscal revenue, funding for cultural undertakings shall be gradually increased, and fiscal and tax preferential policies shall continue to be implemented.
(1) During the Ninth Five-Year Plan period, the value-added tax on seven categories of publications, as well as on books sold by Xinhua Bookstores at the county level and below and by rural supply and marketing cooperatives, as stipulated in the 'Provisions on Continuing to Implement Fiscal and Tax Preferential Policies for Propaganda and Cultural Units' (Cai Shui Zi [1994] No. 089) of the Ministry of Finance and the State Administration of Taxation, shall continue to be levied first and then refunded. The income from the sale of film copies by film studios established with the approval of the State Council shall continue to be exempted from value-added tax. The central and provincial-level fiscal authorities shall continue to allocate budget expenditures based on the actual amount of income tax paid by propaganda and cultural enterprises in the previous year, and establish a special fund for the development of propaganda and culture. The central and provincial-level fiscal authorities shall continue to allocate certain special funds in the budget and incorporate them into the special fund for propaganda and culture development.
If the implementation of fiscal and tax preferential policies is discontinued due to tax system adjustments, the fiscal departments at all levels shall correspondingly resolve the funding issues arising therefrom for propaganda and cultural units through budgetary means.
(2) The subsidy funds for the 'Ten-Thousand-Li Border Cultural Corridor' shall be appropriately increased. A certain amount shall be allocated from the ethnic affairs expenditure and border construction expenditure to support the development of cultural undertakings in remote and ethnic minority areas. Relevant local policies shall also gradually increase investment in cultural undertakings in remote and ethnic minority areas.

IV. Establish and Improve Special Fund Systems
To promote the development of propaganda and cultural undertakings, enhance regulatory capacity, ensure key needs, and standardize fund management, the central and provincial levels shall establish and improve relevant special fund systems.
The sources of special funds shall be fiscal budget funds and extra-budgetary funds such as fees approved in accordance with relevant state regulations. The fiscal departments shall make proper budget arrangements for special funds, and relevant departments shall strictly collect extra-budgetary funds in accordance with regulations. Currently, efforts shall focus on perfecting the systems of 'Special Fund for Propaganda and Culture Development', 'Special Fund for Creation and Performance of Preferential Plays (Programs)', 'Special Fund for National Film Industry Development', and 'Special Fund for Publishing Development'.
Special funds are fiscal funds, and their systems shall be improved and management strengthened in accordance with the requirements of relevant fiscal laws and regulations, ensuring that they are used exclusively for designated purposes and subject to supervision and inspection by the fiscal and audit departments.
